speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand the onset and progression of your symptoms, have you noticed any specific triggers or changes in your environment recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (Group A Streptococcus). The progression from febrile illness to a pruritic rash that involves the trunk and extremities, followed by a facial rash sparing the nose and mouth, is highly characteristic of scarlet fever. REQUEST TEST: Throat_Culture AND Rapid_Strep_Test.
